Side
SYD
n. / v. / adj.
Webster 1828 treats SIDE as noun from Latin latus: the broad part of a surface; margin / verge; the part of an animal between back and belly; the slope of a hill; any part considered by direction; party / faction / sect; interest / favor (The LORD is on my side, Psalm 118:6); opposition; a branch of a family; quarter / region. As adjective: lateral, oblique. As verb: to lean; to embrace the opinions of a party. This page fills the KJV-gap word of place and allegiance. Companion pages already treat lord, blood, and neighbor.

Biblical Definition

Side in Scripture is not a team color and not a personality. It names the place of a body, the place of a neighbor, and the allegiance that will not stay neutral. Moses will not let the camp keep a third option: Who is on the LORD'S side? let him come unto me (Exo 32:26). The psalmist will not let fear write the roster: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me? (Psa 118:6). The Gospel will not let the cross be a metaphor only: one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water (John 19:34). Protection is not a theory: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee (Psa 91:7). The priest is not excused by liturgy: when he saw him, he passed by on the other side (Luke 10:31). The dictionary therefore keeps side from becoming either partisan branding or a body without blood. It is the Bible’s way of saying: here, not there — and whose you are.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines SIDE as the broad part or margin of a thing; the flank of a body; a slope; a party or faction; interest and favor (Psalm 118:6); and as a verb, to take a party. To take sides is to attach oneself to one interest against another.

expand to see more

SIDE, noun [Latin latus.]

1. The broad and long part or surface of a thing, as distinguished from the end.

2. Margin; edge; verge; border; as the side of a river or a road.

3. The part of an animal between the back and the face and belly; the part of which the ribs are situated; as the right side; the left side.

4. The slope, declivity or ascent, as of a hill or mountain.

7. Party; faction; sect; any man or body of men considered as in opposition to another.

8. Interest; favor. The LORD is on my side. Psalm 118:6.

9. Any part being in opposition or contradistinction to another; in the battle, the slaughter was great on both sides.

To take sides, to embrace the opinions or attach one's self to the interest of a party when in opposition to another.

SIDE, verb intransitive. To embrace the opinions of one party or engage in its interest, when opposed to another party.

Key Scripture

Exodus 32:26 — "Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the LORD'S side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him."

Psalm 118:6 — "The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?"

John 19:34 — "But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water."

Psalm 91:7 — "A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee."

Luke 10:31 — "And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side."

Modern Corruption

Side is corrupted when the LORD’s side is recast as a party, when the pierced side is emptied of blood, and when the other side is how the religious pass by a neighbor.

expand to see more

The first corruption is Exodus 32:26 as a caucus. Who is on the LORD'S side? is not a campaign slogan. Partisan religion baptizes a faction and calls it Levi. The recovery is the Name, not the jersey. Psalm 118:6 remains The LORD is on my side — not the other way around as a mascot.

The second corruption is John 19:34 as art. The spear, the side, the blood and water are history. Liberal Protestant talk keeps the wound as a symbol of solidarity and drops the atonement. The dictionary will not. The side was pierced. The blood came out.

The third corruption is Luke 10:31 as professionalism. The priest passed by on the other side. Busy religion, liturgical religion, and online religion all know the move: keep clean, keep moving, keep the neighbor theoretical. Mercy is not a side-quest. It is obedience on this road.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: flank / margin / party / favor. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek pleura (G4125) at John 19:34; Hebrew tsad (H6654) at Psalm 91:7; Greek antiparerchomai (G492) at Luke 10:31 on side. Exodus 32:26 and Psalm 118:6 carry no Strong’s tag on side in this cache; this page does not mint one.

expand to see more

Greek pleura (G4125) — the side of the body (John 19:34, the pierced side).

Hebrew tsad (H6654) — side, flank (Psa 91:7, at thy side).

Greek antiparerchomai (G492) — to pass by on the opposite side (Luke 10:31; the cache tags side with 492 on that verse line).

Exodus 32:26 and Psalm 118:6 are KJV-verified; the cache does not tag side with a Hebrew number on those verse lines. No lemma is invented here.

Usage

"Moses asks, Who is on the LORD'S side? (Exo 32:26); the psalmist answers, The LORD is on my side (Psa 118:6)."

"Christ’s side was pierced; blood and water came out (John 19:34)."

"A thousand may fall at thy side (Psa 91:7); the priest who will not be a neighbor passes by on the other side (Luke 10:31)."
